Present Appeal is filed by the Original Opposite Party aggrieved by the Judgment and Order dated 19th April 2022, in M.A.C.P. No.1799 of 2018, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Mumbai thereby the Appellant was directed to pay Respondent Nos.1 to 5 ("Claimants") the compensation of Rs.48,35,000/- alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim till realisation of said entire amount.
2) The learned Advocate for the respective parties submitted that the Appeal may be finally heard at the stage of admission itself.
Mr.Mehta, the learned Advocate for Respondent Nos.1 to 5 submitted the compilation of documents.
Hence, the Appeal taken up for final hearing.

3) Facts giving rise to this Appeal are that, the claimants filed the said claim therein they averred that, on dated 24/09/2018, at about 1.30 hours, late Mr.Sameer Murlidhar Bankar ("deceased") was riding his motor scooter bearing MH-03-BV-5663 ("scooter") and he was proceeding by Sion Bridge,
North Wahini road.

When the scooter of the deceased reached at Mankikar junction, besides Highway Apartment, Sion, a motor dumper bearing regn. No.MH-01-AN-746 H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc ("dumper") gave a forcible dash to the scooter.
The dumper was driven at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the deceased fell down and sustained serious injuries.
On receiving first information of the accident, Sion Police Station registered the same at FIR No.226/2018, under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC, against the driver of the dumper.
The deceased died on the same day.
3.1) The claimants averred that, the deceased was doing a catering business thereby he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The claimants were dependent upon the income of the deceased.

Therefore,
they prayed to award a compensation of Rs.75,00,000/-.
4) The Appellant opposed the claim by filing the written statement (Exh.11) and denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the dumper.
The Appellant denied that the deceased was doing the catering business and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The Appellant contended that at the time and place of the accident, the deceased was riding his scooter at a high speed, rash and negligent manner and lost control while overtaking the dumper.
As a result, the scooter skidded and came across the right rear wheel of the dumper.
Consequently, the deceased suffered the fatal injuries.

sentences.text: 2 5) Hence, the Tribunal framed the issues.

To prove the claim,
the claimants adduced the evidence on Affidavit of Respondent No.1 (AW1/Exh.14) and Respondent No.5 (AW2/Exh.38).
Besides, the claimants have relied upon various documents in evidence.

In rebuttal, the Appellant produced the evidence of OW1-Vinod Pratap Sankpal, on Affidavit (Exh.42),
who was driving the dumper at the relevant time.
6) On evaluating the evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the dumper.
The deceased was doing the catering business thereby he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The claimants were dependent upon the deceased.
Therefore, the Tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.48,35,000/- with interest.
Hence, the Appeal.
7) Mr. Patil, the learned Advocate for the Appellant submitted that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the scooter by the deceased himself.
In any event, this is case of contributory negligence, where the negligence on the part of the deceased was more.
However, the Tribunal held otherwise, and fasten the entire negligence to the driver of the dumper.

Mr.Patil, the learned Advocate submitted that apart from kachcha receipt and H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc registration certificate of Udyog Aadhar, the claimants have not produced any satisfactory documentary evidence to establish that, indeed the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month by doing the catering business.

According to him, the said income could be maximum Rs.15,000/-,
notionally, as per minimum wages rules prevailing at the time of the accident.
As such, the compensation awarded is on the higher side.
Mr. Patil, therefore, submitted that the impugned judgment and order be modified accordingly.
To support the aforesaid submissions, Mr. Patil cited the following decisions.
I have carefully considered the same.
i) Sushila Devi and Ors. Vs.
Sandeep kumar United Insurance Co. Ltd1.

entities.text: Sandeep kumar United Insurance Co. Ltd1
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In this case the High Court observed and held that, "... rash and negligent driving does not in every case necessarily mean the excessive speed.
Not taking due care while driving the vehicle and in particular overtaking, either stationary or moving vehicle also would amount to rash and negligent driving . ..."
ii) Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Nanded Vs. Habib Khaled Habib Mohammad and Ors.2.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Nanded Vs. Habib Khaled Habib Mohammad and Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case it is held that, "... Accidents take place many times in fraction of seconds.
Only due to the alert
1. (2023) SCC Online Del 1896 2. (2020) 6 Mh.L.J. 214 H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc drivers and their presence of mind, some times they are successful in avoiding the accident.

But in order to have a safe driving the basic principle they are required to adhere is, to have safe distances between two vehicles and then either to cross the road or to overtake the vehicle going ahead of it etc. ..."

iv) Future General India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mumtaz Begum and Ors.4.

entities.text: Future General India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mumtaz Begum and Ors.4

sentences.text: In this case the deceased was running a Tea Stall with Snacks and Tiffing Centre.
The Manager of the Tea Stall deposed that the profit of the Tea Stall would be Rs.25,000/- per month.
There was no document to establish the same.
There were no Income Tax Returns and there was no Bank Statement to establish such an amount of profit in the Tea Stall.
The transaction of the Bank Statement revealed that the income was not clear.
The accurate 3.
(2021) SCC Online Bom 3695 4. (2020) SCC Online Mad 15431 H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc
monthly income of the deceased was not established even through the Bank Statement.
Therefore, the High Court observed and held that the claimants are bound to establish the monthly income of the deceased through some documents.

8) Mr.Mehta, the learned Advocate for the claimants, on the other hand, submitted that there is more than sufficient oral and documentary evidence by the claimants which clearly proved that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the dumper.
Therefore, the said driver stood prosecuted for said crime.
Mr.Mehta submitted that the accident occurred in September 2018.
The family of the deceased comprised of six members including the deceased.
Compared to smaller towns and cities, the personal and living expenses of people living in Mumbai were on the higher side.

Therefore, the Tribunal held that the income of the deceased was Rs.25,000/- per month,
which, in the facts, is reasonable.
As such, there is no substance in the Appeal.
However, Mr. Mehata submitted that in the absence of balance sheet like document, the said income may be taken as Rs.23,000/- per month, but not lesser than that.

9) As to the manner and the cause of the accident, evidence of AW1 is that at the relevant time and place, when the deceased was H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc proceeding on the scooter, the dumper came there, driven at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and gave a forcible dash to the scooter.
As a result the deceased fell down on the road and sustained serious injuries.
The deceased died due to the said injuries.

Since AW1 did not see the accident, her aforesaid narration was supported with the FIR (Exh.16), Spot Panchama (Exh.17), Inquest Panchnama (Exh.18) and Certificate as to the Cause of the Death (Exh.19).
10)
In contrast, the evidence of OW1 is that at the relevant time and place, he was getting off the Sion bridge.
The scooter of the deceased was following and trying to overtake the dumper.
At that point, a group of 8 to 10 bike riders, doing stunts, was heading from the opposite lane from Chembur to Sion.
One of the stunt bikers contacted the scooter of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased lost control and his scooter slipped.
OW1 stated that then he heard a loud noise.
So, he applied the brakes and alighted from the dumper.
Then he saw that the deceased was lying under the right side rear wheel of the dumper, and he was seriously injured.

OW1 contended that he was Municipal Corporation Of Greater ... vs Smita Sameer Bankar And Ors on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190534095/
4 not at fault in the accident.

sentences.text: 10.1) In the cross-examination, OW1 admitted that he did not lodge a counter FIR.
He did not place on record any document H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc contrary to the police statement.
He did not refer the police statement of Respondent No.1, the Spot Panchnama or the Inquest Panchnama.
11) In view of the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred in the middle of the road, and there was no road divider.
There has been no reference of the story of OW1 in FIR and the Spot Panchnam.
The offence was registered against OW1.

However,
no steps were taken to rebut the contention in the police papers.
The Tribunal observed and held that, even if it is accepted that the deceased tried to overtake the dumper from its right side, there was hardly any traffic on the road.
As such, it was for OW1 to drive his heavy vehicle cautiously by taking care of the small vehicle running along with it.
Therefore, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the dumper.
12) In the above context, I have carefully perused the police documents.
The Spot Panchanam recorded that the road where accident occurred was 60 feet wide.
There was no road divider.

The contention of OW1 that about 8 to 10 bike riders were coming from opposite side and doing stunts,
is not mentioned in the FIR or in the Spot Panchnama.
OW1 has not offered any explanation for the said omission.
As such, the story of OW1 that one of the stunt bikers H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc contacted the scooter of the deceased and it led to the accident, is incorrect.
Therefore, it is safe to conclude that at the time of the accident no vehicle was coming from the opposite direction and the deceased had sufficient space on the road to safely over take the dumper.
Nevertheless, OW1 failed to explain as to how the deceased came under the right rear wheel of the dumper.
The FIR clearly mentions that the dumper dashed the scooter.
All these circumstances clearly indicate that OW1 did not keep a proper look at the road while driving the dumper.
As a result the dumper dashed the deceased and caused the accident.
Driving heavy vehicle in such a manner is always dangerous.
The deceased suffered the injuries only when he came under the right rear wheel of the dumper and died due to the said injuries.

Therefore, I am in agreement with the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the dumper in which the deceased sustained the injuries, and consequently died.
13) Now turning to the question as to whether the compensation awarded is excessive or not.
14) In this context, the evidence of AW1 and AW2 is that the deceased was doing the business of catering in the name and styled as H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc "M/s. Shree Sai Sankar Caterers".
He was the proprietor thereof.
This evidence is supported with the Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum/online application for Licence/Renewal of licence under Food and Safety and Standard Act, 2006 (Exh.34).

entities.text: Food and Safety and Standard Act, 2006
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
No doubt, said application was filed in the name of Respondent No.1,
but the application clearly mentions that the catering business was commenced on dated 01.01.2018, and the application was submitted on dated 24.10.2018, i.e., immediately after the death of the deceased.

This fact is sufficient to presume that Respondent No.1 was also involved with the deceased in the said business and therefore, she wanted to continue that business to earn the livelihood for the family.

In other words, unless there was the catering business, Respondent No.1 Municipal Corporation Of Greater ... vs Smita Sameer Bankar And Ors on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190534095/
5 would not have filed that application so promptly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That apart, considering the size of the family, the deceased must be doing some business.
The deceased was maintaining a scooter.
Therefore, I hold that the deceased was doing the catering business.
15) The claimants have not produced the balance sheet or income tax returns of the catering business to establish the monthly income of Rs.75,000/-.
However, AW2, the mother of the deceased produced various payment receipts of purchase of grocery items from H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc various shops, packing materials and utensils etc.
These are Kachcha receipts.

Yet,
the said receipts cannot be ignored and disbelieved.
Because the claimants had no reason to fabricate those receipts.
It appears that the catering business of the deceased may be small.
Therefore, his income may not be so high to attract Income Tax.
15.1) Additionally, it must be noted that the family comprised of six members.
Respondent Nos.5 and 6 were aged.
Respondent No.2 was aged 12 years and she must be a student.
The family has been residing in Chembur, Mumbai.
It is cannot be disputed that, compared to smaller towns and cities, personal and living expenses in Mumbai are on higher side.
Therefore, and in absence of documents like balance sheet, Income Tax return etc., I hold that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.23,000/- per month, which yearly comes to Rs.2,76,000/-.
16) The deceased was aged 37 years as per his date of birth 23/10/1979 appearing on the PAN Card (Exh.28).
His income was not regular.
All the claimants were dependent on the income of the deceased.

Therefore and in accordance with the decisions in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others5 and Sarla Verma and 5. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 6, 40% of the established net annual income should be added towards the future prospects of the deceased and thereafter 1/4 th from the actual net yearly income should be deducted towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma and 5. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicable multiplier is '15'.

Besides, the claimants were entitled to get Rs.40,000/-
each towards spousal, parental and filial consortium.
Additionally, the claimants are entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses'.
Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs.45,77,000/-.
17) Upshot of the above discussion is that, the Tribunal rightly held that the deceased was doing the catering business and that, all the claimants were dependent on the income of the deceased.
However, the Tribunal held the monthly income on little higher side.
Similarly, the Tribunal erred in not awarding the compensation to the minor claimants for the loss of 'parental' consortium and to the father of the deceased for the loss 'filial' for consortium.

The Respondent No.4/father of the deceased expired during the pendency of the claim,
6. 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc but he was represented by the other claimants.
As such, the amount of the 'filial' consortium should be added to the compensation recoverable by the said claimant.
Thus, the impugned Judgment and Order warranted an interference to that limited extent and to modify the award.
The Appeal partly succeeds, accordingly.

sentences.text: (i) First Appeal is partly allowed with proportionate  costs.
(ii) The impugned Judgment and Order dated 19th April 2022, in M.A.C.P. No.1799 of 2018, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mumbai is modified.

(iii) The Appellant- Insurance Company shall pay the compensation of Rs.45,77,000/- (inclusive of NFL amount) together with interest thereon at the rate of 7.5 % per annum from the date of the claim petition till realisation of the amount.

(iv) The entire amount of the compensation alongwith the interest shall be disbursed among the claimants/ Respondent Nos.1 to 3 & 5 and invested in the name of the minor claimants, as directed by the Tribunal.

(v) The balance amount, if any, alongwith proportionate  H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.
interest shall be refunded to the Appellant - Insurance Company.
(vi) Statutory deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal and it be disbursed in accordance with the law.
(vii) The Appeal stands disposed of in above terms.
